title: Build read-only check-in status dashboards from roster, placement, and attendance state
distilled_summary: A read-only Helix dashboard for event or camp check-in should not rely only on the kiosk success screen or registration status. Start with the registration roster, add active non-leader placement group members when the event process allows manual placement outside registration, and derive current check-in state from the latest relevant Attendance row and its AttendanceOccurrence. Display group/location context and event-specific operational fields only from documented models such as placement groups and group attributes. Treat missing placement as a separate operational state, label group-only rows clearly, and suppress registration-only actions when no RegistrationRegistrant exists. Keep the endpoints read-only unless a separate write endpoint is explicitly designed, permissioned, CSRF-reviewed, and audited.

title: Let Helix results partials own table sort state
distilled_summary: For Helix tables with HTMX filters, column sorting, and optional auto-refresh, keep sort state in the server-rendered results partial instead of a custom browser-only variable. Have the partial emit hidden sort and direction inputs, have filter requests include those inputs, and have each sortable header call the results endpoint with its next sort and direction query values. This keeps sorting, filtering, and refresh requests using the same server-side contract. For nullable columns such as room, group, assignment, or last activity, add an explicit null or blank bucket in the server-side ORDER BY so first-click ascending sorts show assigned/actionable values first and blanks at the bottom.
